extracted.intended_audience: graphic designers, marketers, and business professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for designing effective infographics and data visualizations for online marketing, business reports, presentations, and infographic resumes. Emphasizes story structure, design rules, tooling, and distribution/SEO strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make information memorable with creative visual design techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use creative visual design techniques so information is memorable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research shows visual information is more quickly and easily understood, and much more likely to be remembered. The book presents the design process and tools to create infographics that communicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a visual story built with your data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cool infographics tell a story visually — an engaging story built with your data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More than pictures or colorful charts, infographics should create a visual representation that the audience will quickly grasp and remember; the goal is to make the data’s narrative clear and engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure information into a simple 3-part story
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize information using a simple three-part story structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book advises structuring information into a simple 3-part story to make the narrative clear and easy to follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify the design process and follow infographic design rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow an explicit design process and adhere to established infographic design rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify each step of the design process and apply infographic design rules (composition, hierarchy, visual clarity) so the final graphic communicates efficiently rather than merely decorating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose and use effective software tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the best software tools available for creating infographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book presents recommended software tools and techniques for producing infographics, so creators should pick tools that support required visual styles, interactivity, or production workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for the target audience and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Design infographics specifically to reach and serve the target audience and the communication goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether for online marketing, internal reports, or resumes, infographics should be tailored to the audience so the message is quickly grasped and remembered; use visuals appropriate to audience expectations and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement an infographic launch strategy to maximize SEO and reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan distribution and launch (including SEO and social sharing) to maximize the infographic’s visibility and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book covers infographic launch strategies aimed at maximizing SEO value, social sharing, and reaching key influencers; creators should prepare landing pages, sharing links, and tracking to measure results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use infographics for marketing (social media and SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage infographics as online marketing assets, including social media and search engine optimization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers tactics for using infographics in marketing contexts—optimizing for social sharing, search traffic, and integration with marketing strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design an infographic resume to market skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a personal infographic resume that visually markets your skills and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how to design an infographic resume to present professional details visually; be mindful of clarity and whether HR/audience can quickly absorb the information (conciseness matters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply infographics for internal business uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use infographics for internal communications such as board presentations, annual reports, consumer research stats, marketing strategies, business plans, and product/service explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores multiple internal business applications and how infographics can clarify complex information for stakeholders and decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide instructive examples and practical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Use curated examples, good/bad comparisons, and tool/resource lists to learn what works and what to avoid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book includes many examples and links to templates, graphics, and tools; reviewers note value in examples and a 'toolbox' to guide practice, and recommend including both positive and negative examples with captions to explain differences.
